clusters.reason: All four rows are the same component-owned workshop.submit disabled appearance path in the same D0 SwiftUI source, spanning light P1/dark P2 and the two no-valid-selection states baseline/replaced. WorkshopSlotPlanner.swift paints palette.disabled in its label and applies PlainButtonStyle() plus .disabled(selected == nil) to the enclosing button. Its palette declares the approved opaque light/dark disabled colors. Direct original and common-D0 screenshots and frozen sampling reproduce #FFCFCDC5 versus #FFAAA99F in light, and #FF33474C versus #FF52666A in dark. The approved observer host supplies background, viewport and environment without an opacity/overlay/button-style substitution; the bridge only maps fixtures and callbacks. Thus these four correlated manifestations share the same disabled component rendering cause, rather than independent defects per state/theme. The exact internal SwiftUI alpha mechanism is inferred, but common source path, ownership and manifestation membership are directly supported. No Android row is in the confirmed product universe.
